thread:
incident-bot: Paging jamal (oncall): observability.alerts - Sentry event ingestion errors spike detected (rate > 5x baseline) :rotating_light:
jamal (oncall): on it. joining in 30s. any customer reports?
eva (support): ive got 3 cases mentioning missing error reports in the dashboard; customers say recent exceptions not showing up in our triage queue.
maya (SRE): quick note — our alerting pipeline relies on Sentry event counts for a bunch of automated workflows. if Sentry is missing events, incident detection and prioritization will be degraded.
alex (backend): digging into our Sentry forwarding proxy metrics now. preliminary: increased 5xx responses from sentry-main (sentry.io) between 04:04-04:18 UTC.
ops-bot: Forwarded parity: sentry-forwarder-1: 503 x 142, sentry-forwarder-2: 502 x 89, queue-depth: 12k
jamal (oncall): ok. first task: stop automated triage that depends solely on Sentry counts to avoid noisy alerts. maya can you flip the gate?
maya (SRE): doing it now — disabling `sentry-derived-priority` rule in ruleset-service. command:
```
kubectl exec -it svc/ruleset-service -- /bin/sh -c "curl -X PATCH \"http://localhost:8080/rules/sentry-derived-priority\" -d '{\"enabled\":false}'"
```
maya (SRE): applied. will monitor for noise.
eva (support): FYI customers: CUST-214, CUST-87, CUST-412 reported lost exceptions in last ~20m. i've opened high-priority tickets and messaged affected accounts.
leena (product): we need to estimate impact surface: which automations rely on Sentry events? paging? release regressions? can someone list quick?
alex (backend): list: 1) triage queue auto-assign 2) regression alerts (release health) 3) some customer-facing error dashboards 4) anomaly detection pipelines that sample exceptions
jamal (oncall): alex/maya — can we enable internal failover shipping so exceptions are duplicated to our internal S3 ingest? maybe restore visibility even if Sentry is down.
alex (backend): yes. we have a fallback sink `internal-error-sink` used for on-prem. switching on a duplicate write is low-risk. command in prod will be a feature-flag flip: `ERROR_SINK=fallback,sentry`
maya (SRE): I will coordinate the rollout. doing a targeted flip for services with highest error volume first: api-gateway, worker, auth-service.
ops-bot: rollout plan submitted, toggles applied to api-gateway and worker.
jamal (oncall): good. next — contact Sentry status / support. alex, can you grab correlation data: logs showing 502/503 to sentry and sample event ids that didn't get a 200 back so we can provide to them?
alex (backend): collecting now. sample curl showing 503 to sentry endpoint:
```
curl -v -H "X-Sentry-Auth: Sentry sentry_version=7" -X POST https://sentry.io/api/0/projects/redwood/errors/ -d '{"message":"probe"}'
*   Trying 34.203.12.5...
* Connected to sentry.io (34.203.12.5) port 443 (#0)
< HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
< Retry-After: 30
```
alex (backend): also pulling request IDs from our proxy: `req_id=abc123 sentry_resp=503` — collecting full list and will upload to the incident doc.
eva (support): posted the customer-facing blurb in status channel and told CS to acknowledge tickets with "We're aware, working on failover; we may be missing some exceptions temporarily."
leena (product): agree with the blurb. customers care about missed signal and time-to-triage. can we quantify how many exceptions may have been dropped?
maya (SRE): rough method: compare ingest counts to 15m baseline and compute deficit. initial estimate: ~22k events missing across prod in last 20m (~0.6% of daily). i'll post numbers in 5m.
incident-bot: Sentry status page: https://status.sentry.io - current: Partial Outage reported (auth/ingest flapping)
jamal (oncall): escalate to vendor support (Sentry). alex, send telemetry dump + timestamps + sample IDs. include request traces and our queue metrics.
alex (backend): done, support ticket #SNT-19824 created, awaiting response. pasted correlation IDs and our logs.
ops-bot: Pager duty: incident labeled sev3 (third-party degraded) and routed to platform-eng oncall team.
maya (SRE): mitigation summary so far: 1) disabled Sentry-derived automated triage 2) enabled internal fallback sink for critical services 3) notified customers 4) opened vendor support ticket. remaining: determine window of missing events and decide whether to backfill or annotate dashboards.
jamal (oncall): timeline/handoff — I'll keep this incident until 09:30 UTC, then maya will take primary. leave notes in the incident doc.
eva (support): can we produce a priority list of customers to proactively check dashboards for missing regressions? CUST-87 (payment provider) should be top. they were actively debugging a rollback before this.
alex (backend): note: some client SDKs (mobile) have local retries that may resend; server-side proxies are where we saw the 5xxs, so client-side may have partial resubmission. we should not assume all events lost.
maya (SRE): received more numbers — deficit peaking at 29k events over 25m, recovered to 2k/min after 04:22 UTC. estimate final deficit ~18k events. putting exact math in the doc.
leena (product): product ask: can we annotate dashboards to show this data gap so downstream teams don't chase nonexistent regressions? create a visible banner in the console?
jamal (oncall): yes — add a global banner: "We're seeing partial observability gaps for exception data between 04:04–04:30 UTC due to vendor ingest issues. Some errors may be missing."
ops-bot: banner created in console (deploy id dpl-5621).
alex (backend): Sentry responded: "We're investigating an upstream routing issue affecting ingest; retries may be throttled. We're rolling fixes now." Sentry support ETA initial: 30m.
eva (support): pushing proactive messages to affected accounts.
maya (SRE): next steps / actions assigned: - alex: upload telemetry + backfill plan (ETA 2h) - jamal: incident lead until 09:30 (ongoing) - maya: postmortem owner, run root cause triage once vendor confirms (ETA EOD) - ops: confirm fallback retention and ensure duplicate writes went to `internal-error-sink` for needed time window
jamal (oncall): handoff note for maya: watch for delayed regression alerts once we backfill; we may need to suppress automated alerts for 12h to avoid churn.
leena (product): please keep me looped on customer comms timeline; i'll coordinate with growth and enterprise.
incident-bot: reminder — create incident ticket in jira: RDW-INC-2026-041.
maya (SRE): created RDW-INC-2026-041 and added timeline + mitigation steps. linking telemetry artifacts and Sentry ticket.
alex (backend): uploaded log archive and correlation IDs to the incident doc.
jamal (oncall): wrapping up for this shift. leaving detailed notes in RDW-INC-2026-041. maya picking up.
maya (SRE): taking over. next update in 30m or on any vendor change. remember: this is third-party-impact; main risk is triage delay and false negatives in regressions. after vendor fixes we need to assess backfill feasibility and customer-facing remediation.
leena (product): thanks team.
incident-bot: thread closed for on-call handoff (jamal -> maya) at 1771020488"
